causal:influence:abcg5_abcg8_activity:ne.mechanism: The ABCG5/ABCG8 heterodimer in intestinal enterocytes and hepatocytes pumps plant sterols (sitosterol, campesterol) back into the intestinal lumen and bile, limiting their absorption and promoting biliary excretion; loss-of-function of ABCG5 or ABCG8 causes sitosterolemia (OMIM 210250) with marked elevation of plasma sitosterol.

causal:influence:acid_sphingomyelinase_a.evidence: Niemann-Pick A/B OMIM 257200 | intervention: do(SMPD1 activity down) = Niemann-Pick A/B: plasma lysosphingomyelin (SPC) elevated, used as a diagnostic biomarker [citations PubMed-verified]

causal:influence:adipose_tissue_mass:neg.evidence: Diez JJ, Iglesias P. The role of the novel adipocyte-derived hormone adiponectin in human disease. Eur J Endocrinol. 2003;148(3):293-300. PMID:12611609 (PMID verified via PubMed). Inverse relation corroborated by Kern 2003 (PMID:12829646). NOTE: partially mediated by the adipose_tissue_mass -> tnf_alpha -> plasma_adiponectin path; this edge captures the additional TNF-independent hypoxia/hypertrophy component. Both endpoints ORGAN_SYSTEM.
causal:influence:adipose_tissue_mass:neg.mechanism: The adipose paradox: although adiponectin is secreted only by adipocytes, plasma adiponectin FALLS as adipose-tissue mass rises. Hypertrophic/hypoxic adipocytes down-regulate per-cell ADIPOQ (local hypoxia, adipocyte hypertrophy, increased local TNF-alpha/IL-6), and this per-cell suppression dominates the increase in producer-cell number, so net plasma adiponectin decreases. Interventional support: weight-loss / fat-mass reduction raises plasma adiponectin (do(decrease adipose mass) -> increase adiponectin).

causal:influence:adipose_tissue_mass:pos.evidence: "When the amount of adipose tissue increases (signaling excess energy storage), the adipocytes produce increased amounts of leptin, which is released into the blood." — Guyton & Hall, Textbook of Medical Physiology, Ch. 71, p. 867-868
causal:influence:adipose_tissue_mass:pos.mechanism: adipocytes secrete leptin in proportion to fat mass/size, the adiposity signal to the hypothalamus

causal:influence:adipose_tissue_mass:pos.mechanism: increased adiposity raises basal insulin (adiposity-associated insulin resistance / compensatory hyperinsulinaemia)

causal:influence:alpha_mannosidase_activ.evidence: Lehninger Principles of Biochemistry Ch. 7 (N-glycan catabolism; lysosomal mannosidases); Alpha-mannosidosis OMIM 248500; Malm & Nilssen (2008) Orphanet J Rare Dis 3:21 (PMID 18651971): MAN2B1 deficiency causes mannose-rich oligosaccharide storage; urinary oligosaccharides show characteristic mannose-rich peaks on TLC/MS; diagnostic biomarker | intervention: do(MAN2B1 activity ↓) = Alpha-mannosidosis (OMIM 248500): mannose-rich oligosaccharides accumulate in tissues and are excreted in urine [citations PubMed-verified]

When MAN2B1 is deficient (alpha-mannosidosis), mannose-rich oligosaccharides accumulate in lysosomes and are excreted in urine. Enzyme activity inversely predicts urinary mannose oligosaccharide excretion.

causal:influence:alveolar_pco2:positive:.mechanism: arterial PCO2 equilibrates with alveolar PCO2 across the blood-gas barrier; a rise in alveolar PCO2 raises arterial PCO2

causal:influence:alveolar_po2:positive:p.mechanism: low alveolar PO2 acts directly on the small pulmonary arteriole smooth muscle, causing contraction and narrowing; high PO2 dilates

causal:influence:alveolar_surfactant_con.evidence: "surfactant that dramatically lowers the surface tension of the alveolar lining layer and markedly increases the stability of the alveoli" (West's Respiratory Physiology, 11th ed., ch 1)
causal:influence:alveolar_surfactant_con.mechanism: surfactant lowers surface tension and thereby increases alveolar stability

causal:influence:amacr_activity:negative.mechanism: AMACR converts (2R)- to (2S)-methyl-branched acyl-CoA esters (pristanoyl-CoA, bile-acid intermediates) so they can be beta-oxidized; reduced AMACR activity blocks pristanic acid degradation and raises it

causal:influence:amyloid_protein_aggrega.evidence: Mechanism: plaque sequestration of soluble Abeta42 ('sink' hypothesis). Citation VERIFIED: Fagan et al., 'Inverse relation between in vivo amyloid imaging load and CSF Abeta42 in humans', Ann Neurol 2006;59:512-519, PMID 16372280 (confirmed real via PubMed). Review anchor: Blennow & Zetterberg, 'Biomarkers for Alzheimer's disease: current status and prospects', J Intern Med 2018;284:643.
causal:influence:amyloid_protein_aggrega.mechanism: Abeta42 is the most aggregation-prone Abeta species; as fibrillar plaque burden rises it acts as a 'sink', sequestering soluble Abeta42 into insoluble plaque and lowering the soluble CSF pool. do(more aggregation) -> lower soluble CSF Abeta42 (the classic inverse CSF-Abeta42 vs amyloid-PET signature of Alzheimer's disease). Captures the HPO 'Decreased CSF Abeta42' term mechanistically.

causal:influence:angiotensin_II:positive.evidence: PMC10507174 (OVLT/SFO thirst review): ANG II induces thirst/drinking via the SFO; ICV/systemic ANG II is a potent dipsogen. Bourque 2008; Boron & Boulpaep (AngII-induced thirst); HumMod | textbook corroboration: OpenStax Anatomy & Physiology 2e §anp-114 (20.5: Homeostatic Regulation of the Vascular System): 'Angiotensin II also stimulates the thirst center in the hypothalamus, so an individual will likely consume more fluids, again increasing blood volume and pressure.'; OpenStax Anatomy & Physiology 2e §anp-156 (26.3: Water Balance): 'angiotensin II... helps stimulate thirst'; OpenStax Biology 2e §bio-37.3 (37.3: Regulation of Body Processes): 'Angiotensin II in addition to being a potent vasoconstrictor also causes an increase in ADH and increased thirst, both of which help to raise blood pressure.'
causal:influence:angiotensin_II:positive.mechanism: circulating angiotensin II acts on subfornical-organ AT1 receptors to induce thirst and drinking (ICV/systemic ANG II is a potent dipsogen; AT1 antagonists block it)

causal:influence:arginase_activity:negat.evidence: Hyperargininemia (argininemia) OMIM 207800; ARG1 gene; MedLink Neurology — elevated CSF arginine is documented in all ARG1-deficient patients; Lehninger, urea cycle (arginase step 5, arginine -> ornithine + urea). | intervention: do(ARG1 loss-of-function) — hyperargininemia/argininemia OMIM 207800
causal:influence:arginase_activity:negat.mechanism: Arginase (ARG1) hydrolyzes arginine to ornithine + urea; arginine is the substrate. ARG1 deficiency (hyperargininemia) causes arginine to accumulate in plasma and CSF. MedLink Neurology confirms 'increased concentration of arginine is found in the plasma and CSF of all affected individuals' with arginase deficiency.

causal:influence:arginase_activity:posit.evidence: Lehninger, urea cycle (arginase yields ornithine + urea)
causal:influence:arginase_activity:posit.mechanism: arginase produces ornithine from arginine; reduced activity lowers ornithine production

causal:influence:arterial_ph:positive:he.evidence: The O2 dissociation curve is shifted to the right, that is, the O2 affinity of Hb is reduced, by an increase in H+ concentration  ||  "The oxygen dissociation curve moves to the right in exercising muscles because of the increase in PCO2, H+ concentration, and temperature." (West's Respiratory Physiology, 11th ed., ch 9)
causal:influence:arterial_ph:positive:he.mechanism: Bohr effect: an increase in H+ (lower pH) reduces O2 affinity (right shift); higher pH/lower H+ raises affinity

causal:influence:arterial_po2:negative:p.evidence: VHL loss-of-function (von Hippel-Lindau disease; OMIM 193300): constitutive HIF-1-alpha accumulation mimics hypoxia -> VEGF is markedly elevated, driving hemangioblastoma and clear-cell RCC vascularity. Semenza 2003, Nat Rev Cancer (HIF-1/VEGF axis: hypoxia -> VEGF transcription). Ferrara et al. 2003, Nat Med (VEGF regulation by HIF-1 under hypoxia). | intervention: VHL loss-of-function (OMIM 193300): VEGF constitutively elevated; PHD2 inhibitors (hypoxia mimetics) raise VEGF; increasing FiO2 (hyperoxia) lowers VEGF via VHL-mediated HIF-1-alpha degradation
causal:influence:arterial_po2:negative:p.mechanism: Low arterial PO2 (hypoxia) stabilizes HIF-1-alpha (von Hippel-Lindau protein cannot target it for proteasomal degradation under low O2), allowing HIF-1 to transactivate the VEGFA gene; plasma VEGF rises under hypoxia; restoring PO2 restores VHL-mediated HIF-1-alpha degradation and lowers VEGF

causal:influence:aspartoacylase_activity.evidence: Canavan disease (ASPA deficiency, OMIM 271900): pathognomonic massive N-acetylaspartic aciduria — Saudubray, Inborn Metabolic Diseases; Scriver's OMMBID (Canavan disease: NAA acidemia and NAA aciduria are the diagnostic hallmarks); Blau, Physician's Guide to Inherited Metabolic Diseases | intervention: ASPA loss-of-function (Canavan disease)
causal:influence:aspartoacylase_activity.mechanism: Aspartoacylase (ASPA) hydrolyzes N-acetyl-L-aspartate (NAA) to aspartate and acetate in the brain; ASPA deficiency (Canavan disease) prevents NAA catabolism in oligodendrocytes, causing NAA to overflow into blood and urine — reduced ASPA activity raises urinary NAA up to 60-fold above normal

causal:influence:bckdh_enzyme_activity:n.evidence: Lehninger Principles of Biochemistry Ch. 18 (branched-chain amino-acid catabolism; BCKDH oxidative decarboxylation); maple syrup urine disease OMIM 248600
causal:influence:bckdh_enzyme_activity:n.mechanism: the branched-chain alpha-keto acid dehydrogenase complex irreversibly decarboxylates the branched-chain alpha-keto acids; the upstream branched-chain amino acids are the SUBSTRATE pool, so ∂[BCAA]/∂(BCKDH activity) < 0 — LoF (activity DOWN) => BCAA accumulate (MSUD).

causal:influence:beta_galactosidase_acti.evidence: Lehninger Principles of Biochemistry Ch. 21 (ganglioside catabolism; beta-galactosidase cleaves GM1 to GM2); GM1-gangliosidosis OMIM 230500; Brunetti-Pierri & Scaglia (2008) Mol Genet Metab 94(4):391-396 (PMID 18524657): GLB1 deficiency causes GM1 storage in neurons and viscera; substrate confirmed by post-mortem and biopsy assay | intervention: do(GLB1 activity ↓) = GM1-gangliosidosis (OMIM 230500): GM1 ganglioside accumulates in neuronal lysosomes throughout CNS [citations PubMed-verified]
causal:influence:beta_galactosidase_acti.mechanism: GLB1 (lysosomal acid beta-galactosidase) cleaves terminal beta-galactose from GM1 ganglioside (yielding GM2) and from keratan sulfate/lactosylceramide. In GM1-gangliosidosis (GLB1 deficiency), GM1 ganglioside accumulates in neuronal lysosomes. Enzyme activity inversely determines tissue GM1 level.

causal:influence:beta_ketothiolase_activ.evidence: Beta-ketothiolase deficiency (ACAT1, OMIM 203750); Saudubray, Inborn Metabolic Diseases — beta-KT deficiency: urinary 2-methyl-3-hydroxybutyrate is the most reliable diagnostic marker; Fukao et al., Orphanet J. (2004): 2M3HB, 2MAA, and tiglylglycine are characteristic urine organic acids | intervention: genetic LoF of ACAT1 gene (biallelic mutation; autosomal recessive beta-ketothiolase deficiency)
causal:influence:beta_ketothiolase_activ.mechanism: Mitochondrial acetoacetyl-CoA thiolase (ACAT1/T2) cleaves 2-methylacetoacetyl-CoA (the penultimate step in isoleucine catabolism) to propionyl-CoA + acetyl-CoA; ACAT1 deficiency blocks this step, causing accumulation of 2-methylacetoacetyl-CoA and its reduction product 2-methyl-3-hydroxybutyryl-CoA, hydrolysed to 2-methyl-3-hydroxybutyric acid — reduced ACAT1 activity raises urinary 2-methyl-3-hydroxybutyrate

causal:influence:beta_ureidopropionase_a.evidence: Beta-ureidopropionase deficiency OMIM 613161; van Kuilenburg et al., J Inherit Metab Dis 2008. | intervention: do(UPB1 LoF, OMIM 613161) — N-carbamoyl-beta-aminoisobutyrate rises in urine
causal:influence:beta_ureidopropionase_a.mechanism: Urinary N-carbamoyl-beta-aminoisobutyrate is the same compound as ureidoisobutyrate (3-ureidoisobutyrate = CHEBI:1670); UPB1 deficiency causes this metabolite to accumulate in urine.

causal:influence:blood_colloidal_osmotic.evidence: OpenStax Anatomy & Physiology 2e §anp-113 (20.4: Capillary Exchange): 'whereas hydrostatic pressure forces fluid out of the capillary, osmotic pressure draws fluid back in... NFP = CHP - BCOP.'
causal:influence:blood_colloidal_osmotic.mechanism: NFP = CHP - BCOP; blood colloidal osmotic pressure generated by plasma proteins opposes filtration and drives reabsorption, reducing NFP

causal:influence:bronchial_smooth_muscle.evidence: PMID 1537710; (Abstract); “With a steady-state MCh infusion of 2.4 micrograms/min into the bronchial perfusate (perfusate concentration = 0.7 microM), there was an approximate doubling of lung resistance and a 50% fall in dynamic compliance.” | Methacholine-induced bronchial smooth muscle contraction roughly doubled lung resistance, supporting do(bronchial tone up) -> airway resistance up (+). [citations PubMed-verified]
causal:influence:bronchial_smooth_muscle.mechanism: increased bronchial smooth muscle contractile tone narrows airway lumen (decreased diameter) -> increased resistance to airflow

causal:influence:btk_kinase_activity:pos.evidence: XLA (OMIM 300755): absent IgG including all subclasses; Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine, 'X-linked agammaglobulinemia'; Janeway's Immunobiology 10th ed. | intervention: do(BTK LoF) — no B cell maturation, no IgG1-secreting plasma cells
causal:influence:btk_kinase_activity:pos.mechanism: BTK deficiency blocks all B cell development; all IgG subclasses including IgG1 are absent in XLA as no class-switched plasma cells can form.

causal:influence:carboxyhemoglobin:posit.evidence: The presence of COHb also shifts the O2 dissociation curve to the left (Figure 6.2), thus interfering with the unloading of O2
causal:influence:carboxyhemoglobin:posit.mechanism: COHb left-shifts the O2 dissociation curve (raises affinity of remaining sites), impairing unloading

causal:influence:cellular_adp_level:nega.evidence: Mechanism: ADP/AMP rise -> AMPK activation -> ACC1/ACC2 Ser80/Ser221 phosphorylation -> ACC inactivation. Hardie DG, AMP-activated protein kinase: a key regulator of energy balance with many roles in human disease, J Intern Med 2014;276(6):543-559, PMID 24824502 (verified: confirms AMPK phosphorylates both ACC isoforms at equivalent Ser sites, inactivating them and thereby lowering malonyl-CoA, enhancing fatty-acid oxidation). Guyton & Hall, Medical Physiology, 11th ed., Ch. 68 (energy metabolism / fat utilization). ACC is an established direct AMPK substrate; AMPK activation by AMP/ADP and the resulting inhibitory ACC Ser-phosphorylation are demonstrated by perturbation (AMP titration, AMPK activators, non-phosphorylatable ACC mutants) in the cited mechanistic literature.
causal:influence:cellular_adp_level:nega.mechanism: ACC catalytic activity is acutely controlled by cellular energy charge, on top of its ACACA/ACACB gene-dose floor. A rise in cellular ADP/AMP (energy deficit: fasting, exercise, hypoxia) allosterically activates AMP-activated protein kinase (AMPK), which phosphorylates ACC1/ACC2 at the equivalent Ser80/Ser221 sites and inactivates them. So do(increase) in cellular ADP lowers ACC activity. This is a genuine within-CELLULAR allosteric/phosphorylation controller, parallel to the already-encoded cellular_adp_level -> phosphofructokinase_activity energy-charge edge.

causal:influence:core_temperature:positi.evidence: Stolwijk 1971 (sweat command ~ positive core error); HumMod sweat rate control | textbook corroboration: OpenStax Anatomy & Physiology 2e §anp-003 (1.4: Functions of Human Life): 'increased body temperature can cause the responses of sweating … in order to decrease body temperature'; OpenStax Anatomy & Physiology 2e §anp-004 (1.5: Requirements for Human Life): 'One of the body's responses to heat is, of course, sweating.'; OpenStax Anatomy & Physiology 2e §anp-005 (1.6: Homeostasis): 'As blood flow to the skin increases, sweat glands are activated to increase their output'; OpenStax Anatomy & Physiology 2e §anp-026 (5.3: Accessory Structures of the Skin): 'When the body becomes warm, sudoriferous glands produce sweat to cool the body' — body warmth drives eccrine sweat secretion.; OpenStax Anatomy & Physiology 2e §anp-027 (5.4: Functions of the Integumentary System): 'If the body becomes excessively warm... sweat glands will be stimulated by the sympathetic nervous system to produce large amounts of sweat'; OpenStax Anatomy & Physiology 2e §anp-143 (24.7: Energy and Heat Balance): hypothalamus initiates sweating to allow evaporation of water on the skin when temperature is too high; OpenStax Biology 2e §bio-33.3 (Homeostasis): 'The hypothalamus maintains the set point for body temperature through reflexes that cause vasodilation and sweating when the body is too warm.'
causal:influence:core_temperature:positi.mechanism: hypothalamic warm signal drives eccrine sweat secretion above the sweating threshold

causal:influence:cortisol:negative:capil.evidence: Guyton & Hall, Medical Physiology, 11th ed. Ch.77 (Adrenocortical Hormones) §Cortisol Prevents Development of Inflammation: “Cortisol decreases the permeability of the capillaries, probably as a secondary effect of the reduced release of proteolytic enzymes. This prevents loss of plasma into the tissues.”
causal:influence:cortisol:negative:capil.mechanism: cortisol reduces proteolytic-enzyme release and prostaglandin/leukotriene formation, lowering microvascular permeability

causal:influence:cortisol:negative:tnf_a.evidence: Boron & Boulpaep Medical Physiology (glucocorticoid receptor transrepression of NF-kB suppresses cytokines) — primary molecular anchor [citations PubMed-verified]
causal:influence:cortisol:negative:tnf_a.mechanism: glucocorticoid receptor transrepression of NF-kB suppresses macrophage TNF-alpha transcription

causal:influence:cortisol:positive:plasm.evidence: Guyton & Hall — cortisol hyperglycaemia; clinical Cushing's | textbook corroboration: OpenStax Anatomy & Physiology 2e §anp-094 (17.7: The Adrenal Glands): 'their overall effect is to inhibit tissue building while stimulating the breakdown of stored nutrients to maintain adequate fuel supplies'; 'Adrenal hormones also have several non-stress-related functions, including the increase of blood sodium and glucose levels.'; OpenStax Anatomy & Physiology 2e §anp-138 (24.2: Overview of Metabolic Reactions): 'cortisol... its main role is to increase blood glucose levels by gluconeogenesis'; OpenStax Biology 2e §bio-37.5 (37.5: Endocrine Glands): 'These hormones increase blood glucose levels to maintain levels within a normal range between meals.'
causal:influence:cortisol:positive:plasm.mechanism: net effect of raised hepatic output plus reduced peripheral uptake raises glycaemia

causal:influence:crh:positive:pituitary_.evidence: HumMod endocrine (CRH -> ACTH); Boron & Boulpaep HPA axis | textbook corroboration: OpenStax Anatomy & Physiology 2e §anp-091 (17.4: The Pituitary Gland and Hypothalamus): 'The release of ACTH is regulated by the corticotropin-releasing hormone (CRH) from the hypothalamus.'; OpenStax Anatomy & Physiology 2e §anp-094 (17.7: The Adrenal Glands): 'Its secretion is prompted when CRH from the hypothalamus triggers ACTH release from the anterior pituitary.'
causal:influence:crh:positive:pituitary_.mechanism: CRH stimulates corticotrope ACTH (POMC) release from anterior pituitary

causal:influence:csf_pyridoxal_phosphate.evidence: GeneReviews NBK581452 (PNPO deficiency, OMIM 610090); Alghamdi S et al. Clin Genet 2021 — 87-case PNPO deficiency review: CSF HVA/5-HIAA decreased pattern; Blau N et al. Neurology 2001 (CSF monoamine metabolite patterns in B6-responsive disorders); Pons R et al. Pediatr Res 2004 (PLP as AADC cofactor). | intervention: do(PNPO LoF causing pyridoxal-5'-phosphate-responsive seizures, OMIM 610090) [citations PubMed-verified]
causal:influence:csf_pyridoxal_phosphate.mechanism: Pyridoxal-5'-phosphate (PLP) is the obligatory cofactor for aromatic L-amino acid decarboxylase (AADC/DDC), the enzyme that decarboxylates L-DOPA to dopamine and 5-hydroxytryptophan (5-HTP) to serotonin. PNPO (pyridoxine-5'-phosphate oxidase) deficiency impairs conversion of pyridoxine-5'-phosphate to PLP, depleting CSF PLP. Without adequate PLP the AADC holoenzyme cannot form, abolishing dopamine and serotonin synthesis and producing an AADC-like neurotransmitter deficiency pattern (CSF HVA ↓, CSF 5-HIAA ↓, urinary vanillactate ↑). do(PNPO LoF → CSF PLP ↓) → AADC activity ↓.

causal:influence:cyp11b1_activity:positi.evidence: Congenital adrenal hyperplasia due to 11-beta-hydroxylase deficiency (OMIM 202010); MedlinePlus CYP11B1; Clinical, genetic, structural basis of CAH PMC5347606; CYP11B1 mutations and functional consequences PMC3992560; Classic adrenal steroidogenesis PMC9991025. CYP11B1 encodes the enzyme that performs the 11-beta hydroxylation converting 11-deoxycortisol to cortisol in zona fasciculata. | intervention: CYP11B1 LoF (CAH due to 11-beta-hydroxylase deficiency): cortisol secretion from zona fasciculata falls; ACTH stimulation increases CYP11B1 activity -> cortisol secretion increases
causal:influence:cyp11b1_activity:positi.mechanism: CYP11B1 (steroid 11-beta-hydroxylase) catalyses the terminal step in cortisol biosynthesis in adrenal zona fasciculata: converting 11-deoxycortisol to cortisol. CYP11B1 activity is the immediate and direct determinant of cortisol output from zona fasciculata cells; LoF (CAH type due to 11-beta-hydroxylase deficiency) abolishes cortisol production from this step.

causal:influence:cytochrome_b5_reductase.evidence: Hereditary methemoglobinemia types I and II (OMIM #250800): autosomal-recessive LoF mutations in CYB5R3 cause metHb to rise to 10-70% of total haemoglobin depending on type (MedlinePlus Genetics CYB5R3); PMC3075332 (Moura et al. 2011) — two novel CYB5R3 mutations in type I; Lehninger Principles of Biochemistry, 'Hemoglobin: An Allosteric Protein' (metHb reduction by NADH-metHb reductase); Harrison's, 'Methaemoglobinaemia' | intervention: Genetic LoF: homozygous CYB5R3 mutation (OMIM #250800, type I/II recessive congenital methemoglobinemia) — erythrocyte metHb rises to 10-70%; pharmacological inhibition of the NADH pathway by dapsone/nitrites also raises metHb (phenocopies LoF) [citations PubMed-verified]
causal:influence:cytochrome_b5_reductase.mechanism: In erythrocytes, the soluble isoform of CYB5R3 (NADH-cytochrome b5 reductase) transfers electrons from NADH via cytochrome b5 to methaemoglobin (Fe3+ haem), reducing it back to functional oxyhaemoglobin (Fe2+ haem). This is the principal (>99%) pathway for disposal of spontaneously-oxidised metHb. When CYB5R3 activity is reduced, the metHb-to-Hb reduction is impaired and erythrocyte methemoglobin accumulates.

causal:influence:dihydropyrimidine_dehyd.evidence: Lehninger Principles of Biochemistry (Nelson & Cox), Nucleotide metabolism (pyrimidine catabolism: uracil -[DPYD]-> 5,6-dihydrouracil); OMIM 274270 (dihydropyrimidine dehydrogenase deficiency, DPD/DPYD LoF: uracil and thymine accumulate); van Kuilenburg et al. (2001) Clin Chem Lab Med 39:795–798. | intervention: genetic LoF of DPYD (DPD deficiency, OMIM 274270)
causal:influence:dihydropyrimidine_dehyd.mechanism: Dihydropyrimidine dehydrogenase (DPYD) reduces uracil to 5,6-dihydrouracil as the first step of pyrimidine catabolism; higher DPYD activity consumes uracil. LoF (DPD deficiency) causes uracil and thymine accumulation in plasma, urine and CSF.

causal:influence:ebp_activity:negative:p.evidence: X-linked chondrodysplasia punctata type 2 (Conradi-Hunermann-Happle syndrome) / CHILD syndrome, OMIM:302960 — LoF causes accumulation of 8(9)-dehydrocholesterol and related Delta8 sterols in plasma and skin
causal:influence:ebp_activity:negative:p.mechanism: RHEA:15281 (EC 5.3.3.5), physiological direction: 5alpha-cholest-8-en-3beta-ol (8-dehydrocholesterol) -> lathosterol (5alpha-cholest-7-en-3beta-ol); EBP isomerises the Delta8 double bond to Delta7; 8-dehydrocholesterol is the substrate

causal:influence:elovl2_activity:positiv.evidence: Jakobsson et al., J Biol Chem 2006 (ELOVL2 preferred substrate C20:4n-6 -> C22:4n-6); ELOVL2 GWAS variants associated with plasma adrenic acid (Genome-wide metabolomics studies, e.g. Kettunen et al., Nat Commun 2016); Lehninger, Ch. 21 (PUFA elongation). | intervention: ELOVL2 loss-of-function: ELOVL2 LoF -> failure to elongate arachidonic acid (C20:4n-6) to adrenic acid (C22:4n-6) -> reduced plasma adrenic acid [citations PubMed-verified]
causal:influence:elovl2_activity:positiv.mechanism: ELOVL2 (very long chain fatty acid elongase 2) elongates arachidonic acid (C20:4n-6) to adrenic acid (docosatetraenoic acid, C22:4n-6) by adding two carbons. ELOVL2 is the principal elongase acting on C20 polyunsaturated fatty acids. ELOVL2 LoF reduces plasma adrenic acid (and other C22 PUFA) with accumulation of the C20 substrates.

causal:influence:epinephrine:negative:br.evidence: Guyton & Hall, Medical Physiology, 11th ed. Ch.37 (Pulmonary Ventilation) §Nervous and Local Control of the Bronchiolar Musculature: “Both these hormones—especially epinephrine, because of its greater stimulation of beta-adrenergic receptors—cause dilation of the bronchial tree.”
causal:influence:epinephrine:negative:br.mechanism: circulating epinephrine activates beta-adrenergic receptors on bronchiolar smooth muscle -> relaxation -> reduced contractile tone

causal:influence:epo_receptor_activity:p.evidence: "the important effect of erythropoietin is to stimulate the production of proerythroblasts from hematopoietic stem cells in the bone marrow ... the erythropoietin causes these cells to pass more rapidly through the different erythroblastic stages" — Guyton & Hall, Textbook of Medical Physiology, Ch. 32, p. 423
causal:influence:epo_receptor_activity:p.mechanism: activated EPOR stimulates production of proerythroblasts from hematopoietic stem cells and accelerates passage through erythroblast stages

causal:influence:estradiol:positive:hdl_.evidence: "Postheparin hepatic lipase activity is increased by exogenous androgens (and decreased by estrogens), accounting for the decrease in HDL after androgen treatment" — Williams Textbook of Endocrinology, 14th ed., ch 26, p. 1600
causal:influence:estradiol:positive:hdl_.mechanism: estrogens decrease hepatic lipase activity → reduced HDL catabolism → increased HDL-cholesterol

causal:influence:extracellular_fluid_vol.evidence: Guyton & Hall, Medical Physiology, 11th ed. Ch.30 (Regulation of Acid-Base Balance) §Regulation of Renal Tubular Hydrogen Ion Secretion: “Extracellular fluid volume depletion stimulates sodium reabsorption by the renal tubules and increases H+ secretion and HCO3- reabsorption”

causal:influence:mitochondrial_complex_i.evidence: Mitochondrial Complex II Deficiency Nuclear Type 1 (OMIM 252011, SDHA LoF): SDHA mutations abolish Complex II (SDH) activity, leading to reduced overall respiratory chain activity and lactic acidosis; patients show 20-30% residual SDH and succinate-CoQ reductase activity in muscle/fibroblasts. StatPearls Biochemistry: Electron Transport Chain (NBK526105): Complex II transfers electrons from FADH2 to ubiquinone (Q), producing ubiquinol (QH2) that feeds Complex III. Lehninger Principles of Biochemistry ch. 19 (electron transport chain: CoQ as mobile carrier between Complexes II/III and Complex III). | intervention: SDHA/SDHB/SDHC/SDHD loss-of-function (Mitochondrial Complex II Deficiency, OMIM 252011/619166/619167/619224): SDH LoF → Complex II activity reduced → ubiquinol production reduced → Complex III electron input decreased → Complex III activity reduced | intervention: SDHA/SDHB/SDHC/SDHD loss-of-function (Mitochondrial Complex II Deficiency, OMIM 252011): SDH subunit LoF → Complex II activity abolished or severely reduced
causal:influence:mitochondrial_complex_i.mechanism: Complex II (succinate:ubiquinone oxidoreductase / SDH) oxidizes succinate to fumarate and, via its covalently-bound FADH2, transfers two electrons through three iron-sulfur clusters to ubiquinone (CoQ), reducing it to ubiquinol (QH2). Ubiquinol is the mobile electron carrier that delivers electrons to Complex III (ubiquinol:cytochrome c oxidoreductase / bc1 complex). Complex II activity is therefore the rate-controlling step for ubiquinol supply to Complex III: higher Complex II activity → more ubiquinol produced → more electrons available for Complex III → higher Complex III electron-transfer activity. LoF of any SDH subunit (SDHA, SDHB, SDHC, SDHD) reduces ubiquinol production and consequently reduces Complex III flux and overall respiratory chain activity.

causal:influence:mlycd_activity:positive.evidence: Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine, 'Inherited disorders of fatty acid metabolism' — malonyl-CoA decarboxylase deficiency (OMIM 248360); Santer R et al., J Inherit Metab Dis 2003; Wightman PJ et al., Hum Genet 2003; Lehninger Principles of Biochemistry, malonyl-CoA as CPT1 inhibitor and fatty acid synthesis regulation. | intervention: do(MLYCD loss-of-function) — malonyl-CoA accumulates, CPT1 inhibited, LCFA beta-oxidation and ketogenesis impaired

The resulting impairment of hepatic fatty acid oxidation reduces acetyl-CoA supply for ketogenesis, producing hypoketotic hypoglycaemia, as well as cardiomyopathy and skeletal myopathy.

causal:influence:scn_output_rate:positiv.evidence: Reppert SM & Weaver DR Nature 2002;418:935–941 (PMID:12198538): SCN drives melatonin rhythm via sympathetic innervation of the pineal; SCN ablation abolishes plasma melatonin rhythm. OpenStax Anatomy & Physiology 2e §anp-018 (3.5 The Cell Cycle): melatonin circadian rhythm is described; §anp-091: pineal melatonin as circadian regulator — 'the pineal gland secretes melatonin…regulated by the SCN'. | intervention: light-dark reversal shifts the SCN output phase and correspondingly shifts plasma melatonin peak. [citations PubMed-verified]
causal:influence:scn_output_rate:positiv.mechanism: The suprachiasmatic nucleus (SCN) drives nocturnal melatonin synthesis via a multisynaptic pathway: SCN → paraventricular nucleus → superior cervical ganglion → sympathetic noradrenergic innervation of pinealocytes → β1-adrenoceptor/cAMP → AANAT (arylalkylamine N-acetyltransferase) activation → N-acetylserotonin → ASMT/HIOMT → melatonin secretion. Greater SCN nocturnal output (darkness-driven) produces higher plasma melatonin; SCN lesions abolish the melatonin rhythm.

causal:influence:skeletal_muscle_contrac.mechanism: Increasing stimulation frequency causes successive twitches to summate before relaxation; at sufficiently high frequencies, twitches fuse into smooth tetanus, producing maximal tension far exceeding a single twitch. Thus higher contraction frequency (up to the fusion frequency) increases tetanic tension produced by the muscle.

causal:influence:umps_activity:positive:.evidence: Suchi et al., Am J Hum Genet 1997 (UMPS LoF: hereditary orotic aciduria with megaloblastic anemia); OMIM 258900 (hereditary orotic aciduria: UMPS deficiency -> orotic acid accumulation + megaloblastic anemia); Ng et al., Front Genet 2023 (UMPS deficiency: megaloblastic anemia, neutropenia, failure to thrive in infancy); Lecturio Orotic Aciduria (megaloblastic anemia from impaired nucleic acid synthesis in erythroid precursors). Lehninger Principles of Biochemistry (de novo pyrimidine synthesis: UMPS produces UMP for pyrimidine nucleotide pool; essential for DNA replication). | intervention: do(UMPS LoF, OMIM 258900): de novo pyrimidine synthesis blocked at UMP; pyrimidine nucleotide pool depleted; erythroid progenitor DNA synthesis impaired; megaloblastic anemia. | intervention: do(UMPS LoF, hereditary orotic aciduria, OMIM 258900) [citations PubMed-verified]
causal:influence:umps_activity:positive:.mechanism: UMPS (UMP synthase) catalyses the last two steps of de novo pyrimidine biosynthesis (orotate -> OMP -> UMP), providing the UMP precursor for all pyrimidine nucleotides (UTP, CTP, dTTP). UMP is essential for DNA synthesis in rapidly dividing erythroid progenitors. UMPS deficiency (hereditary orotic aciduria, OMIM 258900) blocks de novo pyrimidine synthesis, causing UMP/pyrimidine nucleotide deficiency in erythroid progenitors; impaired DNA synthesis leads to megaloblastic changes, nuclear-cytoplasmic asynchrony, intramedullary apoptosis, and megaloblastic anemia (severely impaired erythroid progenitor proliferation and maturation). Higher UMPS activity ensures adequate UMP supply for erythroid progenitor DNA synthesis.

causal:influence:uroporphyrinogen_decarb.evidence: Harrison's PIM, The Porphyrias (PCT: elevated urinary porphyrins); StatPearls NBK563209; ASH Education Program 2024 (PCT: urine and plasma porphyrins elevated, predominantly uroporphyrin). | intervention: UROD loss-of-function (porphyria cutanea tarda, OMIM 176100)
